summary_of_pdf: This document is an RPost cryptographic proof of delivery receipt memorializing an email transmission from RJ Aguiar to Japanese intellectual property counsel. The underlying communication seeks legal representation and transmits a 47-patent portfolio, three specific USPTO patent applications, a Department of Defense license grant involving Heidi Shyu, and multiple formal criminal referrals and SEC whistleblower disclosures alleging wire fraud and retaliation.
attorneys_comments: This RPost receipt constitutes highly probative, self-authenticating evidence of transmission and actual notice under FRE 901 and FRE 803(6). Tactically, it establishes that AIK Law (Ohno, Katayama) received and opened the transmission, thereby imputing knowledge of the attached patent portfolio, DoD license grants, and explosive whistleblower/criminal referrals. Conversely, the documented SMTP 550 5.4.1 delivery failures to TMI Associates (Ryobu, Hayashi) conclusively negate any presumption of receipt by those individuals. The substantive attachments suggest a highly volatile, multi-forum dispute implicating 28 U.S.C. § 1498 government use claims, DFARS data rights controversies, and SEC whistleblower retaliation. The sender is aggressively papering the record to establish actual notice, likely to support future claims of willful infringement or to exhaust administrative remedies. Counsel must approach this matter with extreme caution given the named government officials and the allegations of interstate wire fraud.
recommended_next_steps: 1. Preserve this RPost receipt and all native attachments in a secure litigation hold to maintain the cryptographic chain of custody. 2. Initiate a comprehensive conflicts check regarding RJ Aguiar, Lockheed Martin, the DoD, and the named individuals (McDonald, Herche, Shyu). 3. Review the identified USPTO applications (19/639,265; 19/639,219; 19/639,255) in Patent Center to assess prosecution status and potential 35 U.S.C. § 154(d) provisional rights. 4. Analyze the purported 'Heidi Shyu License Grant' to evaluate potential 28 U.S.C. § 1498 jurisdictional triggers. 5. Refrain from substantive response until the SEC whistleblower (TCR 17742-648-351-976) and criminal referral liabilities are fully triaged by white-collar defense counsel.
